candidates.attacker_control: File/directory paths or multipart upload file names supplied by a remote user and passed by the application to ESAPI's file validators (directly via ESAPI.validator().getValidFileName()/isValidFileName()/assertValidFileUpload()/getValidDirectoryPath(), or indirectly through DefaultHTTPUtilities.getFileUploads()). For the directory-containment defect, the attacker must be able to influence the `directorypath`/`input` argument; for the file-name defect, they must be able to supply the file name or full path used after validation.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Direct traversal payloads against getValidFileName() appear blocked in this snapshot: (i) line 555 canonicalizes the input and line 556 validates the canonicalized copy against Validator.FileName (ESAPI.properties line 492), which excludes '/' and '\', and getValidInput canonicalizes percent, HTML-entity and JavaScript escapes before matching, so '../', '..\', '%2e%2e%2f', '/' and double-encoded forms are rejected; (ii) literal separators fail the input.equals(cpath) check (lines 564-566); (iii) the shipped upload consumer DefaultHTTPUtilities.getFileUploads() (lines 587-596) takes only the last segment after splitting on [\/\\] before validating and writing, so its own use is not traversable; (iv) I could not construct a payload that passes both the equality check and the FileName regex, so the 'path traversal in getValidFileName' reading is NOT confirmed. The objectively verifiable defect is the containment check at line 469 (prefix comparison without a separator) and the sanitized-value-discarding wrappers. Also checked and not selected: crypto MAC is validated before decryption (JavaEncryptor.decrypt/CipherText.validateMAC), no unsafe Java deserialization or XXE was found (XmlEsapiPropertyLoader sets disallow-doctype-decl), no auth-bypass condition was found in AbstractAuthenticator/FileBasedAuthenticator, and the fail-open ValidationErrorList variants (e.g. DefaultValidator lines 1124-1132) require caller misuse.
candidates.impact: Directory-containment bypass / path traversal leading to file write or read outside the intended directory: integrity impact (overwrite/create files in attacker-reachable sibling directories, e.g. a deploy or config directory sharing the upload directory's prefix) and confidentiality impact (reading files via callers that use the original path), with potential escalation to code execution where the reachable directory is web-served or on the classpath. Scope is limited by the preconditions above (attacker-influenced directory argument, or application reuse of the original path).
candidates.prerequisites: An application uses ESAPI for upload/path validation and (i) passes an attacker-influenced directory path to getValidDirectoryPath()/assertValidFileUpload() while a sibling directory sharing the parent's path prefix exists and is writable, or (ii) validates a client-supplied file path with the boolean/void validator variants and then uses the original (unsanitized) path for file open/write/read. The FileName/DirectoryName regexes must permit the payload shape (DirectoryName explicitly permits '/', '\' and ':'; ESAPI.properties line 493).
candidates.root_cause: ESAPI's file-path containment validation is heuristic rather than explicit. (a) `DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath()` performs its 'dir is inside parent' test as `!dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath())` (line 469) with no path-separator boundary, so a sibling directory whose path merely shares the parent's prefix (e.g. parent `/srv/uploads` vs dir `/srv/uploads-old`) is accepted as being inside the parent. (b) `DefaultValidator.getValidFileName()` (lines 541-581) does not contain an explicit path-separator/'..' rejection: it derives `canonical = new File(input).getCanonicalFile().getName()`, validates a *canonicalized copy* of the input against the `Validator.FileName` whitelist regex (`configuration/esapi/ESAPI.properties` line 492), and requires `input.equals(cpath)` where `cpath` is the basename of the canonical path; for inputs without literal separators this equality is trivially true, so encoder/codec behaviour and the configured regex are the only traversal barriers. (c) The APIs most likely to be used with file writes are `boolean isValidFileName(...)` (lines 517-537) and `void assertValidFileUpload(...)` (lines 820-824), which discard the sanitized return value of `getValidFileName`, so applications following the natural pattern of validating a client-supplied path and then using that original path to open/write a file receive no enforced containment guarantee.
candidates.title: Path-containment bypass in ESAPI file-path validation used for uploads (DefaultValidator.getValidFileName/getValidDirectoryPath)
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker controls an upload file name or a path argument. 2) Application calls ESAPI.validator().isValidFileName()/assertValidFileUpload()/getValidDirectoryPath() (or DefaultHTTPUtilities.getFileUploads(), line 590). 3) getValidFileName() computes the basename of the canonicalized input (line 555), validates the canonicalized copy against the FileName whitelist (line 556) and requires raw-input == canonical basename (lines 558-566); getValidDirectoryPath() accepts any canonical path sharing the parent's prefix (lines 469-471). 4) Because the boolean/void wrappers return no sanitized value (lines 517-537, 820-824), the caller keeps using the original attacker-influenced path when constructing the file to write/read (the shipped consumer at DefaultHTTPUtilities.java lines 596-608 builds new File(finalDir, filename) and File.createTempFile(...)). 5) Files can consequently be created/read outside the directory the application believed was enforced (sibling-prefix directory, or a caller-side traversal path), subject to OS permissions.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; no code was executed and no tests exist in the snapshot. The mapping of this defect to a specific published advisory (e.g. a CVE fixed in a later ESAPI release) is not verified from source or external data, and I could not demonstrate a working exploit for the pure getValidFileName path because the FileName regex + canonicalization + basename-equality check block sibling-prefix traversal there. Whether any real application passes an attacker-influenced directory argument to getValidDirectoryPath/assertValidFileUpload, or reuses the original path after the boolean/void validators, is unverified.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); CWE-41 Improper Path Equivalence (containment check bypass); related CWE-59

coverage_summary: Reviewed the full 301-file visible snapshot structure (215 Java main sources, shipped configuration, docs; no test sources present). P1 index: 286/301 files indexed, 15 files missing from the index, syntax-level containment/call/override candidates only (no data flow, control flow or semantic resolution; 4582 unresolved calls), so indexed relations were used solely for navigation and every cited edge was re-read in source. Manual source review covered: DefaultValidator and all validation-rule classes; DefaultEncoder and codecs (Percent, HTMLEntity, JavaScript, XML, Abstract*); DefaultHTTPUtilities, SecurityWrapperRequest/Response, ESAPIFilter, ClickjackFilter; JavaEncryptor, CipherText/Serializer, CryptoHelper, CryptoToken, KeyDerivationFunction, SecurityProviderLoader, CipherSpec; AbstractAuthenticator, FileBasedAuthenticator, DefaultUser, User; DefaultAccessController, FileBasedACRs, policy loaders; WAF filter, ConfigurationParser, BeanShellRule, SimpleVirtualPatchRule, InterceptingHTTPServletRequest; logging bridges/scrubbers (Java/Log4J/SLF4J); configuration loaders (XML/standard/prioritized); SafeFile, DefaultRandomizer, DefaultExecutor, DefaultIntrusionDetector, StringUtilities, ESAPI/ObjFactory, and the security-relevant ESAPI.properties/validation.properties settings. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: remaining WAF rules/actions, JSP tag classes, localization properties, error classes, and the examples/scripts directories.
limitations: No execution, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were run; findings are source-reasoning only and nothing is runtime-confirmed.
The snapshot excludes test sources, so upstream test expectations for the file-validation methods could not be consulted.
The P1 relation index omits 15 files and provides only syntactic candidates with no data-flow/reachability proof; unreported areas are not claimed as reviewed.
The specific advisory/CVE mapping for this version could not be verified from in-repo or external data (no web access), so the candidate is a lead, not a matched CVE.
Dependency-level vulnerabilities (e.g. commons-fileupload, xom, antisamy versions in pom.xml) were not assessed as source vulnerabilities.

Exploitability of the submitted candidate depends on application-side usage patterns (attacker-influenced directory argument, or reuse of the original path after boolean/void validation), which cannot be confirmed from this library-only snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Direct path traversal via Validator.getValidFileName() (CVE-2022-23457-type claim)
rejected_leads.reason: Could not substantiate a bypass in this snapshot: after getValidInput canonicalization the FileName whitelist regex (ESAPI.properties line 492) rejects '/' and '\', and inputs containing literal separators fail the input.equals(cpath) check at DefaultValidator.java lines 564-566. Reported only as part of the submitted candidate's broader containment finding, with the specific traversal mechanism explicitly marked unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: SafeFile class does not prevent directory traversal
rejected_leads.reason: Explicitly documented non-goal in its own Javadoc (SafeFile.java lines 25-31: 'This does _not_ prevent against directory traversal attacks'), has no callers in the snapshot, and the class is a helper constructor rather than a security decision point; not a vulnerability by itself.

rejected_leads.lead: Fail-open ValidationErrorList variants return the original unvalidated input (DefaultValidator.getValidRedirectLocation lines 1124-1132, getValidListItem lines 883-891, getValidPrintable lines 1017-1028/1079-1090)
rejected_leads.reason: Real fail-open pattern that could yield open redirect/validation bypass if a caller uses the ErrorList variant and ignores the errors list, but exploitation requires application misuse; not selected as the single strongest source-evidenced candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: FileBasedACRs.matchRule(Map, Class, String) returns 'rule != null' instead of rule.allow (lines 218-225)
rejected_leads.reason: Looks inconsistent with the string path variant, but the data-rule file format parsed by loadDataRules() has no allow/deny column (class|roles|actions), so presence of a matching rule legitimately means allow; no concrete privilege-escalation impact established.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak password storage / non-constant-time password comparison in FileBasedAuthenticator (hash.equals(currentHash), line 341; account-name salt, line 423)
rejected_leads.reason: Known documented limitation of the reference authenticator (issue #233 referenced in-file), low practical impact for a reference library, and not attacker-controlled in the sense required here.

rejected_leads.lead: getValidDirectoryPath / getValidFileName symlink handling (canonicalization follows symlinks)
rejected_leads.reason: Noted while tracing the candidate; no concrete write-through-symlink path was established in this snapshot's own code, so it is recorded as an unconfirmed sub-aspect rather than a separate lead.

summary:
Snapshot is OWASP ESAPI (Java) at version 2.2.3.1 (release notes in-tree dated 2021-05-07); 301 visible files, 215 Java main sources, no test sources, plus shipped configuration (ESAPI.properties/validation.properties) and docs. I reviewed the validator/encoder/codec stack, HTTP utilities and servlet filters, crypto (JavaEncryptor, CipherText/Serializer, CryptoHelper, CryptoToken, KDF, SecurityProviderLoader), authentication/user code, access-control rules, WAF filter/rules, logging bridges/scrubbers, configuration loaders, SafeFile, Randomizer and Executor. No auth bypass, MAC-ordering flaw, unsafe deserialization, XXE, command injection or hard-coded key was found; the crypto MAC is verified before decryption and the XML property loader disables DOCTYPE declarations.

The single strongest candidate I can support is a path-containment weakness in ESAPI's file-path validation: `DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath()` decides "dir is inside parent" with a bare `String.startsWith()` on canonical paths (line 469), which accepts sibling directories that merely share the parent's path prefix; and the file-name validation used for uploads (`getValidFileName()`, lines 541-581) only compares the raw input to the basename of the canonicalized file and relies on the FileName whitelist regex to exclude separators, while the boolean/void wrappers (`isValidFileName`, `assertValidFileUpload`, lines 517-537/820-824) discard the sanitized value, leaving the common "validate-then-use-original-name" pattern dependent on that regex alone.

Important counterevidence: I could not construct a pure `../`/`..\` traversal that passes `getValidFileName()` in this snapshot. After `getValidInput(...,"FileName",255,true)` canonicalizes percent/HTML/JS encodings, the `Validator.FileName` regex in ESAPI.properties (line 492) rejects `/`, `\` and control characters, and inputs containing literal separators fail the `input.equals(cpath)` check at line 564; `DefaultHTTPUtilities.getFileUploads()` (line 587-596) also reduces the client-supplied name to its last path segment before validating and writing. The candidate is therefore submitted as a lead (CWE-22/41 containment-bypass) with low confidence in exploitability, not as a confirmed traversal.
